sections.content: In units 13 to 15 you saw that a Hungarian verb keeps its stem and changes its ending for each person. The stem is the form in the vocabulary list: *olvas*. “I” takes *-ok / -ek / -ök*. “You” (one friend) takes *-sz*, but *-ol / -el / -öl* after a stem ending in *s, sz* or *z*. He, she or a name takes no ending. “We” takes *-unk / -ünk*, “you all” takes *-tok / -tek / -tök* and “they” takes *-nak / -nek*. The vowels of the stem choose, as they do for *-ban/-ben*.

sections.title: Pronouns, no and questions
sections.content: The ending says who acts, so the pronoun is usually left out. Say *én, te, mi, ti* or *ők* to set people side by side: *Mi főzünk, ők pihennek.* *Nem* goes right before the verb. A friend asks about *you* and you answer about *me*: *Olvasol?* – *Igen, olvasok.* After *ki* the verb is the plain stem: *Ki olvas?*
Add no ending after a name: *Anna olvas*, never *Anna olvasok*. And answer *Olvasol?* with *Olvasok*, not *Olvasol*: the answer is about you.
